decisions.reason: Font adjustment is only one possible way to balance article endings; the source decision does not necessarily alter the separate requirement that body text must not appear too light or frail.
The candidate governs breaking up excessive uninterrupted text, while the source addresses conspicuous whitespace at article endings; its existing treatment remains valid unchanged.
Allowing advertisements as possible whitespace-balancing elements does not change the independent requirement that advertisements render clearly without blurriness.
Article-ending whitespace balance does not necessarily change the flipbook deliverable or its two-page-spread display behavior.
The source decision about balancing article endings does not alter author-name or author-photo requirements.
Whitespace balancing may affect layout work, but the source does not necessarily change the table-of-contents completion condition or page-number accuracy requirement.
The permitted techniques for balancing article endings do not change the magazine's brand alignment, general visual style, or red-color usage rules.
Using images as possible whitespace-balancing elements does not modify the independent requirement to enhance image quality when needed.
The article-ending standard does not change the digital launch target or its established deadline.
